Package hadur117.core.duel

Class HandOffDesign

java.lang.Object
hadur117.core.duel.HandOffDesign
public final class HandOffDesign extends Object
The endgame hand-off switches (HAND-1 to HAND-3): what the duel plays when it takes over from the melee with one opponent left, off a team. Each is a ship-time constant the bench builds an arm from (build-ablation.sh); all off. None acts in a 1v1 (the duel never takes a hand-off there) or on a team (the duel is told it is on one), so the duel and team play are untouched by construction.

Live, 23% of Hadur's melee rounds are lost in that endgame duel and only 46% of them are won against the top 30 (docs/bench/live-3.20-melee.md). The duel there plays plain: no 1v1 mode table, no shield, and nothing the melee learned about the survivor's gun.

    HAND-2 (arm edge): when the melee's book says the survivor's gun is head-on (at least 3 hits on Hadur this battle, 60% of them within Hadur's width of head-on), the dodge planner is on against it for the endgame, primed with the head-on expert.
    static final boolean
    ENDGAME_LEARNED_SHIELD
    HAND-3 (arm eshd): the same verdict starts shield mode against the survivor on SHIELD-15's trial, listed or not; the trial's exits leave it for the battle once it fails.
    static final boolean
    ENDGAME_MELEE_GUN
    HAND-5 (arm emgun): in the endgame duel, the melee's field gun aims and fires at the survivor in place of the duel gun, while its kNN history of the survivor is deep enough to be a learned aim (the field gun's own test).
    static final boolean
    ENDGAME_TABLE
    HAND-1 (arm etab): the survivor's entries in the 1v1 mode table apply in the endgame as in a duel: the shield list (shield mode, with the list's opening drive, shipped aims and exits), the simple-aim dodge, the dodge planner, stop-and-go, heat-jit and the gun stack.

    • ENDGAME_CLOSE

      public static final boolean ENDGAME_CLOSE
      HAND-4 (arm eclose): the endgame duel starts at ENDGAME_CLOSE_OPENING px, not the opening book's distance (650 px for a survivor with no 1v1 profile, which is most of them), and DIST-1 moves it from there. On the 1.11.2 cloud census (docs/bench/melee-top3.md) the endgame duel is fought at a median 694 px with power 1.0 and a 14% hit rate, against 40% in the crowd, and is lost 21% of the time against survivors ranked below 30th, almost always from behind on energy. Closer, Hadur's gun (the better one in most endgames) gains more than the survivor's.

    • ENDGAME_MELEE_GUN

      public static final boolean ENDGAME_MELEE_GUN
      HAND-5 (arm emgun): in the endgame duel, the melee's field gun aims and fires at the survivor in place of the duel gun, while its kNN history of the survivor is deep enough to be a learned aim (the field gun's own test). The field gun has watched the survivor all battle and keeps reading its scans in the duel; the duel gun has only the endgames' few hundred ticks. The duel still moves and runs the radar. On the 1.11.2 cloud census Hadur wins 43% of its endgame duels against top-10 survivors even when ahead on energy.
